vcu_0159_080011ac.name: vcu_udiv64_shift_subtract
vcu_0159_080011ac.summary: 64-bit unsigned divide returning the quotient by 64-step shift and subtract
vcu_0159_080011ac.description: Unsigned 64-bit division by restoring shift-and-subtract, producing one quotient bit per step from bit 63 down to bit 0. At step k it tests (dividend >> k) >= divisor, which is the same as dividend >= divisor << k; when true it subtracts divisor << k from the dividend and adds 1 << k to the quotient. The shifts are done by __aeabi_llsr and __aeabi_llsl, and the remainder stays in the local dividend and is not returned. There is no zero-divisor check, so a zero divisor gives an all-ones quotient. Callers are vcu_0159_0800b440, vcu_0159_0800e8e0 and vcu_14a_080013a0.
vcu_0159_080011ac.notes: The name is ours: the routine resembles libgcc __udivdi3 but was not matched to it. Only the quotient is returned.

vcu_0159_08001240.name: vcu_buf_zero
vcu_0159_08001240.summary: Zero-fill a byte buffer by calling the memset helper with value 0
vcu_0159_08001240.description: Clears param_2 bytes starting at param_1 by calling the ARM EABI helper __aeabi_memset (dest, count, value) with value 0. vcu_0159_08001768 uses it to clear its five 32-bit ADC accumulators (20 bytes). There is no bounds check, so the caller must supply at least param_2 bytes.

vcu_0159_08001244.name: memset
vcu_0159_08001244.summary: C library memset: fill n bytes at dst with c and return dst
vcu_0159_08001244.description: Standard C memset(dst, c, n) argument order. It forwards to the ARM EABI helper __aeabi_memset, which takes (dst, n, c), swapping the value and count arguments, and returns the original destination pointer. The fill byte is param_2 and the count is param_3.

vcu_0159_080012d2.name: __aeabi_i2f_v148_159
vcu_0159_080012d2.summary: Soft-float convert signed 32-bit integer to IEEE-754 single, round to nearest even
vcu_0159_080012d2.description: Signed 32-bit integer to float32 conversion in soft-float form. It takes the absolute value using the sign mask, normalises it with a count-leading-zeros shift, and packs exponent 0x9D minus clz (the top mantissa bit adds the final +1), the top 24 bits as mantissa, and the sign in bit 31. Rounding is to nearest, ties to even: bit 0x80 is the guard, the low 7 bits are the sticky test, and the LSB is cleared on an exact tie. Input 0 returns 0. The packet also lists __aeabi_ui2f (vcu_0159_080012e4) as a callee, so the unsigned core is shared.

returns.description: IEEE-754 binary32 bit pattern in r0

vcu_0159_080012d2.notes: Named with a build range (148, 14b, 14e, 14f, 152, 153, 159; not 14a) because the VCU_14a-only copy vcu_14a_080012ba already uses __aeabi_i2f and names must be unique. Same algorithm as that copy.

vcu_0159_08001348.name: __aeabi_d2iz
vcu_0159_08001348.summary: Soft-float convert double to signed 32-bit integer, truncating toward zero
vcu_0159_08001348.description: Converts an IEEE-754 double (low word param_1, high word param_2) to int32 with truncation toward zero. The biased exponent is bits 30:20 of the high word. Exponents below 0x3FF (|x| < 1) give 0. For 0x3FF <= e < 0x434 the 53-bit mantissa (implicit one at bit 20 of the high word) is shifted right by 0x433 - e to get the integer part. For e >= 0x434 the low mantissa word is shifted left by e - 0x433 with no saturation. A set sign bit negates the result. There is no NaN or overflow handling.

vcu_14a_080013a0.name: crt_init_then_main_v148_14a
vcu_14a_080013a0.summary: Builds 148 and 14a start: run init hook table, call app main thunk, then divide loop
vcu_14a_080013a0.description: Present only in builds 148 and 14a, with no direct callers, so it is an entry point reached by pointer or from reset. It runs the two-record hook table at 0x0800E70C, calling each record as fn(a, b, c) with the three stored arguments, the same pattern as vcu_0159_080016ec. It then calls thunk_FUN_0800ce08, which the family map names app_main_thunk. The decompiler shows a 64-bit shift-and-subtract loop after that call, using FUN_080012F4 and FUN_08001312 as shift helpers and returning the quotient in r0:r1 like vcu_0159_080011ac. The operands come from registers the decompiler could not follow, so the loop may be a decompiler artifact.

returns.description: loop quotient in r0:r1 (only reached if the main thunk returns)

vcu_14a_080013a0.notes: Open questions: whether thunk_FUN_0800ce08 returns; the names of FUN_080012f4, FUN_08001312 and thunk_FUN_0800ce08 are not established in this packet; the 14a table at 0x0800E70C is not verified against the 0159 table.

vcu_0159_08001450.name: __aeabi_dadd
vcu_0159_08001450.summary: Soft-float double-precision add or subtract with exponent alignment and rounding
vcu_0159_08001450.description: Soft-float IEEE-754 double addition (__aeabi_dadd). Subtraction uses the same routine with one operand's sign flipped. The operands are (low, high) word pairs; the larger magnitude is moved to the high side by comparing exponents and mantissas, and the smaller mantissa is shifted right with sticky bits via __aeabi_llsl and __aeabi_lasr when the exponent difference is below 64. Same-sign operands are added and differing signs are subtracted. A cancellation of two or fewer bits is normalised and rounded by vcu_0159_0800164e; otherwise the result is normalised inline. A zero operand returns the other operand, and no explicit NaN or infinity handling is visible.
vcu_0159_08001450.notes: The identification as __aeabi_dadd is inferred from the structure; the decompiled return type is only 32 bits wide, the 64-bit result is in r0:r1.

vcu_0159_0800164e.name: fp64_round_pack
vcu_0159_0800164e.summary: Soft-float double normalise, round to nearest even and pack for the add routine
vcu_0159_0800164e.description: Helper called only from the cancellation path of __aeabi_dadd (vcu_0159_08001450). It takes a 64-bit mantissa with exponent and sign, counts leading zeros to normalise it, and shifts it into the 53-bit double field with __aeabi_llsl and __aeabi_llsr, collecting shifted-out bits as a sticky flag. Rounding is to nearest, ties to even, using bit 10 of the extended mantissa as the guard and bits 0 to 9 as the tie test; a round-up carry propagates into the exponent. An underflowing result returns 0, and overflow is not handled.

params.name: param_2
params.description: mantissa high word including the exponent field

vcu_0159_0800164e.notes: The argument meanings are inferred from the single caller in vcu_0159_08001450.

vcu_0159_080016ec.name: crt_init_then_main
vcu_0159_080016ec.summary: C runtime start: run the two-record init hook table, then call the app main thunk
vcu_0159_080016ec.description: Runtime start called from the reset path after the clocks are set up. It walks the two-entry table at 0x0800F294 to 0x0800F2B4, calling each record as fn(a, b, c) with its three stored arguments. It then calls thunk_FUN_0800d858 (app_main_thunk, the application main entry) and never returns: the decompiler marks the following bad-instruction halt. This routine does not parse a scatter table or copy RAM sections itself, so the earlier description of Reset_Handler as copying RAM sections only holds if the hook records do that work.
vcu_0159_080016ec.notes: Callee names come from the existing app_main_thunk and Reset_Handler annotations. The hook records were not decoded in this packet.

vcu_0159_08001768.name: vcu_adc_average_16_scans
vcu_0159_08001768.summary: Average 16 ADC scans of 5 channels from the DMA buffer into five 16-bit results
vcu_0159_08001768.description: Averages the ADC1 DMA ring buffer at 0x200032A6 into five 16-bit results at 0x2000329C to 0x200032A4. The buffer holds 16 scans of 5 halfword channels (80 halfwords, filled by the circular DMA set up in vcu_0159_08001c3c). It zeroes five 32-bit stack accumulators, adds every halfword of each channel across all 16 scans (step 5), then stores (sum >> 4), which is the truncated mean, into each result and clears the accumulator. The result index follows the rank order from vcu_0159_08001d5c: channels 7, 9, 8, 4 and 5. It has no direct callers in the harness list, so it runs via a pointer or the main loop.

vcu_0159_08001ba8.name: vcu_tmr2_ch1_pwm_start
vcu_0159_08001ba8.summary: Program TMR2 channel 1 PWM frequency, then enable the channel 1 output
vcu_0159_08001ba8.description: Starts the TMR2 channel 1 PWM output. It calls tmr2_pwm_set_frequency (vcu_0159_08001b78), which programs the period and the 3/4 compare value, then sets TMR2 CCTRL bit 0 (C1EN, channel 1 enable) with a read-modify-write, leaving the other channel bits unchanged. The packet's register reference TMR2.CTRL1 is wrong for this offset: 0x40000020 is TMR2.CCTRL. Callers are vcu_0159_08002d64, vcu_0159_08006ae0 and vcu_0159_08006b24.
vcu_0159_08001ba8.notes: The register offset was checked against the at32f415 register table: CCTRL is at 0x20 and C1EN is bit 0.

vcu_0159_08001c3c.name: vcu_adc_dma_ring_init
vcu_0159_08001c3c.summary: Set up DMA1 channel 1 as a circular ADC1 result buffer of 80 halfwords
vcu_0159_08001c3c.description: Initialises DMA1 channel 1 to move ADC1 conversion results from the ADC1 data register (0x4001244C) into the RAM buffer at 0x200032A6 in circular mode. It enables the DMA1 clock (AHBEN bit 0), resets the channel, loads dma_default_para_init, and then sets peripheral-to-memory direction, a fixed peripheral address, memory increment, halfword widths on both sides, circular loop mode and medium priority, with buffer size 0x50 (16 scans of 5 channels). It calls dma_init and then dma_channel_enable(1), so the channel runs from this point.
vcu_0159_08001c3c.notes: The field values follow the dma_init_type offsets documented on the existing dma_default_para_init annotation.

vcu_0159_08001ca8.name: vcu_adc_analog_pins_init
vcu_0159_08001ca8.summary: Set PA4, PA5, PA7, PB0 and PB1 as analog inputs for ADC1 channels 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9
vcu_0159_08001ca8.description: Configures the five ADC inputs, PA4 (ADC1 IN4), PA5 (IN5), PA7 (IN7), PB0 (IN8) and PB1 (IN9), which are the channels used by the ADC1 scan in vcu_0159_08001d5c. It enables the IOMUX, GPIOA and GPIOB clocks, then calls gpio_default_para_init and gpio_init for each port. The packed configuration word is built from the register arguments param_3 and param_4, which the caller does not set, so the exact mode is inferred from the channel mapping as analog.
vcu_0159_08001ca8.notes: The mode is inferred, not decoded: the caller passes no arguments, so the config word is whatever the registers hold on entry.

vcu_0159_08001d5c.name: vcu_adc1_scan_init
vcu_0159_08001d5c.summary: Initialise ADC1 for a 5-channel DMA scan, calibrate it, then start conversion
vcu_0159_08001d5c.description: Brings up ADC1 as the 5-channel scan source for the averaging code. It calls vcu_adc_analog_pins_init and vcu_adc_dma_ring_init, enables the ADC1 clock (APB2 bit 9), and sets the ADC clock divider code 2 with crm_adc_clock_div_set. It writes the base configuration 0x05000101 via adc_base_config (scan on, continuous on, right aligned, ordinary length 5), then sets ordinary ranks 1 to 5 to channels 7, 9, 8, 4 and 5. It selects trigger source 7 (adc_ordinary_conversion_trigger_set), enables DMA requests and the ADC, runs calibration reset and calibration while polling both status flags, and starts the first ordinary conversion by software.
vcu_0159_08001d5c.notes: Two of the adc_ordinary_channel_set calls show only three arguments in the decompile, so their sample-time argument is not visible here. Trigger source 7 is taken to be the software-start selection.

vcu_0159_08001e30.name: vcu_gpio_pa0_init
vcu_0159_08001e30.summary: Configure PA0 as a GPIO input with packed word 0x01080400 and enable the GPIOA clock
vcu_0159_08001e30.description: Enables the GPIOA clock and configures pin 0 (PA0) through gpio_default_para_init and gpio_init, using the packed mode word 0x01080400. The word has no pull and drive strength 1, which matches the SDK default drive. It is called from vcu_0159_08001e6c and from vcu_14a_08001af0. The purpose of PA0 is not visible in this routine.
vcu_0159_08001e30.notes: The input direction is inferred from the packed word; the function's use of PA0 is unknown.

vcu_0159_08001e7c.name: vcu_usart2_pins_init
vcu_0159_08001e7c.summary: Configure PA2 and PA3 as USART2 TX and RX pins
vcu_0159_08001e7c.description: Enables the GPIOA clock and configures PA2 (pin mask 0x4) with packed word 0x01080400 and PA3 (mask 0x8) with packed word 0x01001804 through gpio_default_para_init and gpio_init. PA3 gets a pull-up setting (0x18) and PA2 none. These are the standard USART2 pins, and the DMA setup in vcu_0159_08001f50 and vcu_0159_08001fbc targets the USART2 data register at 0x40004404. The mapping is inferred from the pins and their use, not from a name in the code. It is called from vcu_0159_08001ee8.
vcu_0159_08001e7c.notes: PA3 is also configured as EXINT line 3 in vcu_0159_080026f0 (vcu_exint3_pa3_init). The two have different callers, so they are presumably not used together.

vcu_0159_08001f50.name: vcu_usart2_rx_dma_init
vcu_0159_08001f50.summary: Set up DMA1 channel 6 as the USART2 receive DMA into a 250-byte circular buffer
vcu_0159_08001f50.description: Configures DMA1 channel 6 (control block 0x4002006C) to receive from USART2.DT (0x40004404) into the 250-byte RAM buffer at 0x20002EB4. It enables the DMA1 clock, resets the channel, and sets peripheral-to-memory direction, a fixed peripheral address, memory increment, byte widths, circular loop mode and high priority, with buffer size 0xFA. It calls dma_init and then dma_channel_enable(1). This is the receive half of the USART2 DMA pair with vcu_0159_08001fbc.
vcu_0159_08001f50.notes: Channel 6 as USART2 RX follows the usual DMA1 request map; it was not checked against the SVD.

vcu_0159_08001fbc.name: vcu_usart2_tx_dma_init
vcu_0159_08001fbc.summary: Set up DMA1 channel 7 as the USART2 transmit DMA from RAM, left disabled
vcu_0159_08001fbc.description: Configures DMA1 channel 7 (control block 0x40020080) for memory-to-peripheral transfers to USART2.DT (0x40004404), with the source buffer at 0x200030A8. The buffer size is set to 0 here and must be written before each transmit. It uses normal (non-circular) mode, memory increment, byte widths and high priority. It clears the channel 7 transfer-complete flag (0x02000000), then calls dma_channel_enable with 0, so the channel stays disabled until a transmit sets its count and enables it.
vcu_0159_08001fbc.notes: Channel 7 as USART2 TX follows the usual DMA1 request map. The flag value is the channel 7 transfer-complete bit in the DMA flag map.

vcu_0159_08002030.name: vcu_systick_timebase_init
vcu_0159_08002030.summary: Select the core clock for SysTick and derive the ticks-per-us and ticks-per-ms globals
vcu_0159_08002030.description: Sets SysTick to count the core clock with no divider (systick_clock_source_config with code 4) and derives the time-base globals used by delay_us and delay_ms. DAT_200018B0 becomes the core clock in MHz (the frequency in Hz at 0x200018BC divided by 1,000,000), and DAT_200018B4 becomes the ticks per millisecond (MHz times 1000). The core clock frequency must already be stored at 0x200018BC when this runs. It is called from the init sequence vcu_0159_08002060.

vcu_0159_080020a4.name: vcu_exint14_pb14_init
vcu_0159_080020a4.summary: Route PB14 to EXINT line 14 as a falling-edge interrupt on EXINT15_10, store a probe result
vcu_0159_080020a4.description: Configures a group of GPIO pins (PB2, PB10 to PB14, PF6, PA1) and routes PB14 to external interrupt line 14 with gpio_exint_line_config(GPIOB, 14). It sets line 14 as an interrupt on the falling edge with exint_init, clears its pending flag with exint_flag_clear, and enables the EXINT15_10 IRQ (number 40) with nvic_irq_enable. It finally stores the result of vcu_0159_08007a9c in DAT_20001FEB, which is not described yet.
vcu_0159_080020a4.notes: Falling edge follows the exint_init polarity encoding (value 1). The meaning of the stored value depends on vcu_0159_08007a9c, which is not in this packet.

vcu_0159_080021c4.name: vcu_exint_pb12_pb14_init
vcu_0159_080021c4.summary: Route PB12 and PB14 to EXINT lines 12 and 14 as falling-edge interrupts on EXINT15_10
vcu_0159_080021c4.description: Configures the pins PB2, PB10, PB11, PB12, PB13, PB14 and PA1 with gpio_default_para_init and gpio_init, giving PB14 a pull-up setting (0x18). It routes PB12 and PB14 to EXINT lines 12 and 14 with gpio_exint_line_config(GPIOB, 12) and (GPIOB, 14), sets both lines as falling-edge interrupts with exint_init (line mask 0x5000), and enables the EXINT15_10 IRQ (number 40) with nvic_irq_enable. It does not clear pending flags. It is called from vcu_0159_0800688c.
vcu_0159_080021c4.notes: This routine and vcu_0159_080020a4 both configure PB14 for EXINT14; they have different callers and the one that runs is determined by the caller.

vcu_0159_080022d4.name: vcu_gpio_outputs_set_levels
vcu_0159_080022d4.summary: Drive 15 GPIO output pins to their start-up levels with the set and clear registers
vcu_0159_080022d4.description: Sets the start-up level of 15 output pins using gpio_bits_reset (CLR register) and gpio_bits_set (SCR register). Driven low: PA10, PA11, PA6, PA9, PB6, PB7, PC14, PC15 and PF6. Driven high: PA12, PA15, PB3, PB4, PB5 and PC13. The pins are configured elsewhere in the init sequence, and the function is called from vcu_0159_0800688c.
vcu_0159_080022d4.notes: The pins' functions (power, enable or reset lines) are not determinable from this function. Levels here differ from vcu_0159_0800248c for PA10, PA11 and PA8, which are used by a different init path.

vcu_0159_08002370.name: vcu_can1_clock_disable
vcu_0159_08002370.summary: Disable the CAN1 APB1 peripheral clock
vcu_0159_08002370.description: Clears the CAN1 clock enable (APB1ENR bit 25) by calling crm_periph_clock_enable with enable 0. It is the counterpart of the CAN1 clock enable in vcu_0159_080027f0. It is called from vcu_0159_0800688c.

vcu_0159_0800237c.name: vcu_gpio_out_pins_config
vcu_0159_0800237c.summary: Configure nine GPIO pins on ports A, B and C with packed config words
vcu_0159_0800237c.description: Enables the IOMUX and GPIOA, GPIOB and GPIOC clocks, then configures PA10, PA11, PA12, PC14, PC15, PB15, PA8, PC13 and PA6 through gpio_default_para_init and gpio_init. Most pins use packed word 0x01100400, and PA6 uses 0x01102800. The call is one of two pin-group setups, and vcu_0159_0800248c calls it and then drives the levels. The decompiler shows four argument registers that the caller does not set, so the word values are recorded rather than fully decoded.
vcu_0159_0800237c.notes: The per-pin mode bytes are overwritten by the routine, so only the pin masks are certain.

vcu_0159_0800248c.name: vcu_gpio_board_init
vcu_0159_0800248c.summary: Board GPIO bring-up: configure the port A/B/C pin group, set levels, then init PA9 and PB6/PB7
vcu_0159_0800248c.description: Board GPIO bring-up for one hardware variant. It calls vcu_0159_0800237c to configure the nine-pin group, then drives PA10, PA12 and PA8 high and PA11, PC13, PC14, PC15 and PA6 low. It then calls vcu_0159_08002674 to configure PA9, PB6 and PB7. The caller is vcu_0159_08002060, the init sequence.
vcu_0159_0800248c.notes: Levels differ from vcu_0159_080022d4 for PA10 (high here, low there), so the two are different variants of the same board setup.

vcu_0159_080024fc.name: vcu_spi_pins_remap_init
vcu_0159_080024fc.summary: Remap and configure SPI pins PB3, PB4, PB5 and PA15 before SPI2 setup
vcu_0159_080024fc.description: Enables the IOMUX, GPIOA and GPIOB clocks, applies pin remap code 0x28140401 with gpio_pin_remap_config (enable 1), and then configures PB3 (mask 0x8), PB4 (0x10), PB5 (0x20) and PA15 (0x8000) with gpio_default_para_init and gpio_init. The pins are configured as alternate-function outputs or inputs with packed words 0x01081800 and 0x01101800, and PA15 is set through a 0x110 word. It is called first in vcu_0159_080025b8 (SPI2 init).
vcu_0159_080024fc.notes: The remap target is not decoded. The pin set is the usual SPI remap group, but that is inferred.

vcu_0159_080025b8.name: vcu_spi2_init
vcu_0159_080025b8.summary: Initialise SPI2 from the SDK default config with two overridden words, then enable it
vcu_0159_080025b8.description: Brings up SPI2: it calls vcu_spi_pins_remap_init for the pins, enables the SPI2 clock (APB1 bit 14), and loads spi_default_para_init (slave, full duplex, 8-bit, software chip select). It overrides two init words, 0x00020100 and 0x01000000, then calls spi_init(SPI2) and spi_enable(SPI2, TRUE). The overridden words are not decoded to specific bit fields here.
vcu_0159_080025b8.notes: Whether SPI2 ends up master or slave depends on the overridden words, which were not decoded. Confirm the role before relying on this summary.

vcu_0159_08002674.name: vcu_gpio_pa9_pb67_init
vcu_0159_08002674.summary: Configure PA9, PB6 and PB7 with pull-up words, then drive PB6 and PB7 low
vcu_0159_08002674.description: Enables the GPIOA and GPIOB clocks and configures PA9 (mask 0x200) and PB6 and PB7 (masks 0x40 and 0x80) with the same packed word 0x01101800, which includes a pull-up setting, through gpio_init. It then drives PB6 and PB7 low with gpio_bits_reset. The peripheral that uses these pins is not configured in this function. It is called from vcu_0159_0800248c and vcu_0159_080047ac.
vcu_0159_08002674.notes: PA9 is the default USART1 TX pin and PB6/PB7 are common USART1 or I2C1 pins; neither is confirmed here.

vcu_0159_080026f0.name: vcu_exint3_pa3_init
vcu_0159_080026f0.summary: Route PA3 to EXINT line 3 as a falling-edge interrupt on EXINT3 (IRQ 9)
vcu_0159_080026f0.description: Configures PA3 (mask 0x8) as an input with a pull-up (0x18) through gpio_init, and routes it to EXINT line 3 with gpio_exint_line_config(GPIOA, 3). It sets line 3 as an interrupt on the falling edge with exint_init, enables the line in INTEN with exint_interrupt_enable, clears its pending flag, and enables IRQ 9 (EXINT3) with priority 1. It is called from vcu_0159_0800688c.
vcu_0159_080026f0.notes: PA3 is also USART2 RX in vcu_0159_08001e7c. The two have different callers, so they are presumably not used together.

vcu_0159_08002778.name: vcu_can1_pins_remap_init
vcu_0159_08002778.summary: Remap CAN1 onto PB8 (RX) and PB9 (TX) and configure both pins
vcu_0159_08002778.description: Enables the GPIOB and IOMUX clocks, applies remap code 0x2C000402 with gpio_pin_remap_config (enable 1) to move CAN1 onto PB8 and PB9, and then configures PB9 (mask 0x200, packed word 0x01080400, no pull) and PB8 (mask 0x100, pull-up 0x18) with gpio_default_para_init and gpio_init. The remap is taken as the CAN1 alternate mapping. It is called from vcu_0159_080027f0 (CAN1 init) and vcu_0159_08002980.
vcu_0159_08002778.notes: The remap register bit it changes is not decoded here. PB8 as RX and PB9 as TX are inferred from the CAN1 init that follows.

vcu_0159_080027f0.name: vcu_can1_init
vcu_0159_080027f0.summary: Initialise CAN1: remapped pins, bit timing, six accept-all filters, RX0 and SE interrupts
vcu_0159_080027f0.description: Full CAN1 bring-up. It calls vcu_can1_pins_remap_init, enables the CAN1 clock (APB1 bit 25), and zeroes the can_base_type with can_default_para_init. It fills the base configuration (normal mode, TTC off, AEBO off, AED on, PRSF off) and calls can_base_init, which enters freeze mode. Bit timing comes from can_baudrate_default_para_init with values set to divider 9, RSAW 1, BTS1 10 and BTS2 3 (1 + 10 + 3 = 14 time quanta per bit) and is written by can_baudrate_set. It then configures six receive filter banks (0 to 5) with can_filter_init: each is enabled, 32-bit, identifier-mask mode, FIFO 0, with identifier and mask both zero, so all identifiers pass. It enables NVIC lines CAN1_RX0 (IRQ 20) and CAN1_SE (IRQ 22) and sets interrupt enables with can_interrupt_enable for masks 0x2, 0x400, 0x800 and 0x8000. The bit rate depends on the APB1 clock, which this function does not set.
vcu_0159_080027f0.notes: Which interrupt bit each mask (0x2, 0x400, 0x800, 0x8000) selects is not verified. The bit rate is not computed because the APB1 clock is not known here.

vcu_0159_080028e0.name: vcu_watchdog_start
vcu_0159_080028e0.summary: Start the independent watchdog with divider 256 and reload 1249 (about 8 s at 40 kHz)
vcu_0159_080028e0.description: Configures and starts the independent watchdog. It unlocks register writes (wdt_register_write_enable(1)), sets the prescaler to code 6 (divide by 256, wdt_divider_set), sets the reload value to 0x4E1 = 1249 (wdt_reload_value_set), reloads the counter (wdt_counter_reload), and then writes 0xCCCC to WDT.CMD to start it. The main loop must feed the watchdog afterwards, and vcu_0159_0800d858 calls wdt_counter_reload. It is called from the init sequence vcu_0159_08002060.
vcu_0159_080028e0.notes: The timeout of about 8 s is 1250 x 256 / 40000 and assumes a 40 kHz LSI clock, which is not checked here.

vcu_0159_08002904.name: CAN1_RX0_IRQHandler
vcu_0159_08002904.summary: CAN1 RX FIFO 0 interrupt: read one frame when FIFO 0 has a message and dispatch it
vcu_0159_08002904.description: Interrupt handler for CAN1_RX0 (IRQ 20). If the FIFO 0 message-count flag is set (can_flag_get code 9, RF0MN), it reads one frame from FIFO 0 with can_message_receive into a 20-byte stack buffer and calls vcu_0159_08007bb0 with that buffer, which is the CAN frame dispatch routine and is not described yet. Only one frame is taken per interrupt, and a frame still pending raises the interrupt again.

vcu_0159_08002930.name: CAN1_SE_IRQHandler
vcu_0159_08002930.summary: CAN1 status and error interrupt: latch bus-off, error counters and last error code
vcu_0159_08002930.description: Interrupt handler for CAN1_SE (IRQ 22). It reads CAN1.ESTS (0x40006418). If the bus-off flag (ESTS bit 2) is set it writes 1 to DAT_2000185B. If the error type record is nonzero (can_flag_get code 4, ESTS bits 6:4), it stores the transmit error counter (bits 23:16) in DAT_2000186F, the receive error counter (bits 31:24) in DAT_20001870, and the last error code (bits 6:4) in DAT_20001858. It then clears status flags 3 and 4 with can_flag_clear. Nothing else in this handler reads those RAM bytes.
vcu_0159_08002930.notes: The ESTS field layout was checked against the at32f415 register table: REC 31:24, TEC 23:16, ETR 6:4, BOF bit 2.

vcu_0159_080029d0.name: vcu_fault_0f_update
vcu_0159_080029d0.summary: Update the displayed fault code 0x0F for a state: clear it, or store it when the state is 3
vcu_0159_080029d0.description: Maintains fault code 0x0F as the displayed code. If bit 11 of DAT_20001AEC is set, it clears the displayed code if it is 0x0F (vcu_error_code_clear_if_current) and returns. Otherwise, if param_1 is not 3, it also clears the displayed 0x0F. Only when param_1 is 3 and bit 11 is clear does it store 0x0F as the current fault code without touching the bitmap (vcu_fault_code_store). Callers are vcu_0159_0800a15c, vcu_0159_0800a1d0, vcu_0159_0800a264, vcu_0159_0800a39c and vcu_0159_0800a5c8.

params.name: param_1
params.description: state argument; 3 means store the code

vcu_0159_080029d0.notes: The meaning of fault code 0x0F and of bit 11 of DAT_20001AEC is unknown; the function is described for its effect on the displayed code.

vcu_0159_080029f4.name: vcu_flag_bitmap_expand
vcu_0159_080029f4.summary: Detect changes in three 16-bit flag words and expand set bits into an item index list
vcu_0159_080029f4.description: Watches three 16-bit flag words (current values at DAT_20001CE0, CE2 and CE4). When any of them differs from its last copy (DAT_200022C8, CA and CC), it copies the new values to the last copies and to working words DAT_2000148A, C and E, zeroes the list count DAT_200021E4, sets the pending flag DAT_200022D6, and calls app_set_state(2). While the pending flag is set, it expands each working word into the item list at DAT_200021E8: bit i of the first word adds i+1, of the second adds i+0x11, and of the third adds i+0x21, giving up to 48 items in order. The working words are shifted to zero as they are read, and the pending flag is not cleared here.
vcu_0159_080029f4.notes: The meaning of the flag words and the item numbers is not established in this packet.
